sampling_model.design: The headline theorems use balanced complete randomization, uniform over assignments with exactly \(n=N/K\) units in each arm. The open kernel problem ranges only over laws in \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\): every realized allocation has those fixed counts and every unit has marginal arm probability \(1/K\), without exchangeability.
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) units and all \(K\) potential outcomes per unit are fixed; there is no super-population sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The assignment vector \(Z\) is the sole random object and is generated by the known complete-randomization law or the known admissible nonexchangeable law \(p\).
sampling_model.overlap: Each arm has known marginal assignment probability \(1/K\) and a positive fixed allocation count.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The identification theorem conditions on the armwise empirical marginal laws \(F\); empirical estimation of those margins is outside the first structural kernel and follows the quantile plug-in route of Aronow, Green, and Lee.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The upper bound is attained if the two potential outcomes are comonotonic.
An integer program computes a worst-case copula for broad designs and estimators.
Multi-marginal optimal transport gives exact identified sets for general quadratic cross-world objectives.
The design-based framework permits arbitrary multi-arm contrast matrices.
Supermodular expectations are monotone in concordance for distributions with fixed marginals.
The identity permutation is optimal for a Robinson similarity and dissimilarity when one is Toeplitz.
Isotone imputation converges to a least-favourable two-arm limiting experiment.

body.tldr: Under balanced complete randomization, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) if and only if the contrast Gram matrix \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian. This yields an \(O(K^2)\) certificate, an exact \(K=3,N=6\) worked calculation, and an explicit binary counterexample outside the cone. A second exact boundary shows that common ranks dominate the entire multi-contrast covariance matrix only for a rescaled single pairwise contrast. The open research step characterizes identity-optimality only among covariance tensors induced by valid fixed-count, marginally balanced assignment laws, modulo common unit relabelling, and seeks a polynomial cut certificate with an exact failure witness.

project_justification.gap: Sharp rank completion is analytic for the two-arm difference-in-means estimator, whereas generalized causal-bootstrap work uses integer programming for broad designs and estimators. The literature does not state the exact contrast-geometry boundary at which one common-rank completion remains universally least favourable in a multi-arm experiment, nor a label-invariant recognition problem restricted to realizable nonexchangeable balanced covariance kernels.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator. It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone for complete randomization, a stronger classification for joint covariance dominance, and an admissible moment-polytope domain on which the nonexchangeable recognition problem has statistical meaning.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the complete-randomization risk decomposition, proves the graph-Laplacian iff theorem by pairwise rearrangement and isolated binary necessity witnesses, evaluates both mechanisms exactly at \(K=3,N=6\), classifies the Loewner case, and uses cut generators to characterize the identity-optimal cone over covariance tensors induced by valid balanced assignment laws modulo unit relabelling.

body.related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee establish the two-arm comonotone sharp endpoint; Proposition 4 recovers that result exactly. Imbens and Menzel use the same isotone completion to obtain a least-favourable limiting experiment. Zhao and Ding supply the arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance identity used in Lemma 1 but do not optimize its unidentified cross-arm terms. Tchen's supermodular-order theorem supplies the pairwise rearrangement ingredient, so the proposal does not claim a new general dependence inequality. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, while Brennan et al. compute generalized causal-bootstrap completions by integer programming; both inform the search for a certificate that avoids instance-specific optimization. The open problem takes as its domain only covariance tensors in the exact finite moment-polytope image of balanced assignment laws, rather than arbitrary quadratic-program coefficient arrays. Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz quadratic-assignment theorem supplies the cut-decomposition model for this open nonexchangeable-kernel extension, not a theorem-level result that the present proposal claims to sharpen.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate concerns a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\). It does not turn that scalar endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued covariance bound. Theorem 3 makes this distinction formal: except for a rescaled pairwise contrast, no single common-rank completion can dominate every linear combination simultaneously.
body.honest_scope: The complete-randomization cone theorem should be attainable by combining the published covariance identity with rearrangement and a new necessity classification; its novelty is the causal contrast geometry and Loewner boundary, not the underlying supermodular inequality. The \(K=3,N=6\) propositions are exact audit certificates rather than additional asymptotic claims. The assignment-kernel characterization in Open-ended Question 6 is the first-class unresolved component and is posed only for covariance tensors induced by valid fixed-count, marginally balanced laws, modulo common unit relabelling. Whether every failure in that feasible domain has a binary separator is part of the open question. The proposal does not claim finite-sample tail dominance, empirical-marginal inference, or a closed form outside the certified cone.
